text:
Liam O'Rourke: Heads up—customer reporting missing audit log events for API key rotation. They rotated a key in Console yesterday and don’t see any `api_key.rotate`-type event in their export. This is a blocker for their security review.

Liam O'Rourke: Jira is SUP-4921. Dropping link + notes in thread.

Jira: Created/updated issue SUP-4921: "Enterprise prospect requests confirmation of audit log coverage for API key rotation and RBAC changes" https://jira.redwoodinference.com/browse/SUP-4921

Rachel Kim: Adding a bit more detail from the customer email: they see create + revoke events, but rotation is missing (or shows up sometimes). They’re pulling via S3 export, filtering by `event_name` prefix `api_key.`.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Thanks. First suspicion: we have two rotation code paths (new RBAC service vs legacy token service) and only one is instrumented.

Amara Diallo: +1. Gateway has both routes still in prod. If they used the older “rotate” endpoint, request might bypass the new emitter.

Liam O'Rourke: Customer says they rotated from Console (Settings → API Keys → Rotate). Not sure which backend it hits.

Nadia Rahman: Can someone paste a request_id / approximate timestamp? Want to confirm in pipeline (ingest vs export) before we assume missing instrumentation.

Rachel Kim: They didn’t send request_id. Timestamp from their side: ~2024-06-06 17:20 UTC. They’re in us-east.

Rafael Mendes: If it’s exporter delay/backlog, they’d usually still see it eventually. But they’re saying it never showed up.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: I’ll check logs in staging + prod for `RotateApiKey` handler usage and whether we emit audit events in both. If we’re missing one path, I’ll cut a hotfix.

Amara Diallo: I can confirm which endpoint Console calls. I’ll look at the console-backend route mapping.

Naomi Feldman: Please prioritize—this is coming up a lot in questionnaires. Even if it’s “legacy path,” we need consistent coverage for rotation.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Found it. Console rotate calls `POST /v1/keys/{id}:rotate` which is still handled by legacy token svc in one environment flag config. That handler emits a metrics log but no audit event.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Newer path `POST /v2/api-keys/{id}/rotate` does emit `api.api_key.rotate` (schema v1). So depending on org/env rollout, rotation audit coverage is inconsistent.

Rafael Mendes: That explains “sometimes.” Do we have dual-write on the legacy handler? Or just missing completely.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Missing completely. I’ll add event emission there + a regression test, and route should include actor + request_id.

Amara Diallo: Confirmed from console-backend: it prefers v2 but falls back to v1 when the org isn’t on the new API key service (feature flag). So we need the legacy handler fixed.

Liam O'Rourke: Great. Once we have a PR number, I can update SUP-4921 + tell the customer we have a fix in flight + timeline.

GitHub: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18563 "Hotfix for missing audit event on one API token rotation code path; adds regression test and incident reference"

Kaitlyn Nguyen: PR 18563 is up. Adds audit emission on legacy rotate path, includes `actor`, `org_id`, `request_id`, and `outcome=success|failure`. Also adds a test that rotates via v1 endpoint and asserts event presence.

Nadia Rahman: Please make sure it hits the schema validator (and registry) so we don’t end up with a one-off event name.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Yep—using existing `api.api_key.rotate` event name, same payload shape. No new event name.

Rafael Mendes: Any risk of duplicate events for orgs already on v2? (i.e., both handlers firing?)

Amara Diallo: Should be mutually exclusive based on routing. Console calls one endpoint per request. No fan-out.

Naomi Feldman: Once merged, can we backport to current prod release branch? And note it in beta comms.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Plan: merge today, backport to `release-2024.24`, deploy ASAP. I’ll comment in SUP-4921 with the PR + expected rollout.

Liam O'Rourke: Thanks all. I’ll reply to the customer: confirmed gap on a legacy rotation path, fix is in PR 18563 and we’ll notify when it’s deployed. (reactions: :thumbsup: from Rachel Kim, :white_check_mark: from Naomi Feldman)

Rafael Mendes: After deploy, we should validate via S3 export end-to-end (rotate key, ensure event shows up in sink within SLO). If needed I can run the check.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. I’ll ping once it’s in prod.
